messages.subject: Re: mark-resight and b compatability?
messages.body_plain:
Just to expand on Murray's comment: " There is no mechanism or code for a learned response from one sighting to the next.",

the challenge here is that you don't know which captures are first vs. subsequent captures. You can account for this uncertainty if using MCMC for estimation, in principle, though it is complicated and I don't have any canned software to point anyone to do this. Also, if the magnitude of the behavioral response is large, the posterior uncertainty can be extreme.

The basic idea is that you must update both the true capture history and each individual's first and subsequent capture events (at each trap if trap specific Mb) if those change when you update the true capture history. There is nimble code to do that in the link below in the context of another latent ID SCR model. You can do the same thing for spatial mark-resight or any other latent ID SCR model. But, it's quite complex to implement and you may end up with unhelpfully imprecise parameter estimates (but maybe that is really the situation we face using SMR with a behavioral response to capture)

https://github.com/benaug/Random-Thin-MVHyper

messages.subject: Estimating density using a set sigma value
messages.subject_clean: Estimating density using a set sigma value
messages.body_plain:
Hi Murray/all,

I hope you are doing well.

My name is Paolo Strampelli, and I am a researcher focussing on lions at the NGO Panthera. I had a question for which I was not able to find an answer in the package documentation.

Is it possible to fit a model and estimate density using a pre-set value of sigma that we can define in the code? i.e. estimate density from a capture history and trap layout file, but instead of estimating sigma from these data - and using this to then estimate density - it estimates what the density would be if sigma was this pre-defined value.

I hope I've explained myself clearly - please let me know if not. I also realise this may not be possible, but I thought I'd check if this was something that had been developed already.

Thanks in advance for any assistance.

All the best,
Paolo

messages.subject: Re: mark-resight and b compatability?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Ben. I'm happy to keep out of mark-resight complexity where I can.

'secr' should not have crashed in this case. I have added a check in the next release - it aborts with a message if the mark-resight model includes any learned response. A learned response within the marking phase should be manageable, but would need some special coding, and I'd rather just block learned responses in general for mark-resight data.

Dusit's data gave me another problem that I don't fully understand. With the default (automatic) starting values the Nelder-Mead method for likelihood maximisation sometimes stops at a bad estimate that is not even a local maximum as far as I can tell by plotting the likelihood surface. The Newton-Raphson method simply fails with default starting values. Given reasonable starting values both methods get to about the same likelihood and estimates.

Multi-session data may now be fitted with  parameters for the initial density and session-on-session rate of increase (lambda) (see secr-trend.pdf <https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/secr-trend.pdf>). messages.body_plain:
Hello Lawrence

I don't think this has anything (directly) to do with the choice of detection function. Your data are counts on a single occasion per session, with a 'usage' effort adjustment. For some reason that I have yet to pin down, secr.fit gags on this with other settings at their defaults. I can make it work by ignoring usage (details = list(ignoreusage = TRUE)) or by suppressing the 'fastproximity' default (details = list(fastproximity = FALSE)). The density and sigma estimates are virtually identical between these, only lambda0-hat differs (as expected: usage is in the range 0-1 and lambda0 per unit time/effort is increased). You do not gain from fastproximity when there is already a single occasion per session, so it is safe to switch it off (it is a bug that it was internally 'on' in this case).

Asides - I see you have all-negative detector coordinates; that is unusual but probably not a problem. The detection parameter is 'lambda0', which is unfortunately easy to confuse with other 'lambda's such as the finite rate of increase that appears as a parameter in its own right in secr 4.6.4 (via the Dlambda parameterisation).

Cheers
Murray
